subject: Logic
title: Quine's Paradox
description: A quick, practical guide to Quine's Paradox.

hook.text: "Yields falsehood when preceded by its quotation" yields falsehood when preceded by its quotation.

buildup.text: Willard Van Orman Quine crafted a liar-like paradox without using words like "true" or "false" directly.

discovery.text: The sentence quotes itself by description rather than by name—sidestepping usual restrictions on self-reference.

twist.text: Quine showed that banning self-reference by name doesn't prevent self-referential paradoxes.

climax.text: Self-reference is deeper than quotation marks. Language always finds a way to refer to itself.

quiz.question: How does Quine's paradox achieve self-reference?
options: By describing itself without naming itself
